item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: In inventory-client, update listItems(transport) to resolve to every item, in order, by requesting GET /items and following next_cursor until it is null or absent. Pass the cursor back unchanged; the first request sends no cursor. Add tests with a fake transport covering multi-page results, a single page, an absent next_cursor, and order preservation. Update the README to document the paginated behaviour. Make python3 -m unittest and npm test pass. Commit the change; do not push. Do not change git identity settings.

state.summary:
listItems in inventory-client now follows GET /items cursor pagination. It sends no cursor first, passes next_cursor back unchanged, stops on null or absent, and resolves to all items in order. A failed page, a repeated cursor or a missing items array rejects, so no partial list is returned. Committed as b2e72c9 on archon/3jr23z7f-make-listitems-follow-cursor-pagination (not pushed). Checks: npm test passes 10/10 (3 before; the 7 new tests cover multi-page, single page, absent next_cursor, order, first-request-no-cursor, failures, and repeated cursor). Against the old client.js, 5 of the 10 fail, so the new tests exercise the change. python3 -m unittest does NOT pass: it exits 5 with "NO TESTS RAN", because this repo is Node-only with no Python tests. I did not invent Python tests; this needs a decision from you (drop the item for this repo, or name the Python test to add). README documents the paginated behaviour. Review: one reviewer (agt_01M7W99X7M77JK8T0M1JJMSFRZ) passed head b2e72c9 with no blocking findings, risk medium confirmed. Two non-blocking follow-ups: (1) client.js has no page cap, so a server that keeps issuing new cursors makes listItems run unbounded; (2) the README's pre-existing 'ordered by id' claim is the server contract, which client.js does not itself enforce. pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no cursor first and then next_cursor unchanged. It rejects on a non-200 page, a non-string cursor, a repeated cursor (guards against infinite loops) or a response without an items array, so partial results are never returned. Key files: client.js, test/client.test.js (fake transport keyed by cursor, records requests), README.md. Checks: npm test 10/10 pass; new tests fail on old code (5 of 10). python3 -m unittest exits 5 because the repo has no Python tests; this is a brief mismatch, flagged for decision. Assumptions: the brief's 'python3 -m unittest' does not apply to this Node-only repo. Follow-ups (non-blocking, from review): no page cap on the loop; README 'ordered by id' is the server contract, not enforced client-side.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across pages. now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, in order. before: only the first page of GET /items.
pr.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination

risk.why: Contained behaviour change to listItems and its tests: callers now get every page, meaning more requests and a different result for large inventories. Failures are explicit rejections, not silent partial results. Reviewer agt_01M7W99X7M77JK8T0M1JJMSFRZ confirmed medium.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response); body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items ordered by id; next_cursor null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add tests covering paging through all items, default limit, bounds of limit, and invalid cursor and limit. Update the README to document the parameters and response shape. Make python3 -m unittest and npm test pass. Commit the change; do not push. Do not change git identity settings.

state.summary:
Added cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api, committed as 6e591d4 on archon/b9e8d5pb-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items (not pushed). The change: optional limit (1..100, default 20), opaque cursor (base64 of the last returned id), response {"items", "next_cursor"} ordered by id, and 400 {"error": "..."} for invalid limit or cursor. Also added README docs, 7 new tests, and a package.json whose test script runs python3 -m unittest. Checks on the final head (tree 6aadb19): python3 -m unittest 10 OK (before: 3 OK); npm test 10 OK (before: failed with "Missing script: test"). Risk is high: GET /items with no params now returns 20 items, not all, which is intended by the contract but breaks existing callers. pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination on item id. Cursor is base64url of the last returned id; the next page holds ids greater than it. Invalid limit (non-ASCII-digit, out of 1..100) and invalid cursor (bad base64, non-digit payload) raise ValueError in the parsers and become 400 in list_items. Files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _parse_cursor, _encode_cursor), test_api.py (default limit, paging through 57 items in pages of 10, last page null cursor, exact multiple, cursor past end, limit bounds, invalid cursor), README.md (parameters, response shape, example), package.json (new; test script python3 -m unittest so npm test works). Checks: python3 -m unittest 10 tests OK; npm test 10 tests OK. Assumptions: the repo had no package.json, so npm test was added with the minimal script. Known gaps: oversized digit strings return Python's int-conversion message in the 400 body (status correct); a decorative assert remains in list_items; inventory-client is out of scope. Reviewers: 3 read-only reviews at head 6e591d4, all PASS, no blocking findings.
pr.summary: made GET /items paginate: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and opaque cursor; response has next_cursor (null on last page). before: GET /items returned every item; now: returns one page of up to 20 items plus next_cursor, and invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with an error body.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: API behaviour change: GET /items without params now returns 20 items and a next_cursor key instead of all items, so existing callers silently truncate. Intended by the contract, but breaking with no versioning. Touches api.py, test_api.py, README.md, package.json. Behaviour changes in list_items; tests run with 10 OK on both suites. Reviewers confirmed high.
